channel.title: Pratik Dhanave — Blog
channel.description: Long-form writing on multi-agent AI, medical AI governance, HIPAA-aware architecture, and cloud-native systems.

item.title: Agentic Software Engineering in Go: Introduction
item.description: Vibe coding generates code that works once; agentic engineering builds systems that work forever. This series introduces the five pillars — context engineering, specification engineering, AI-TDD verification loops, autonomy calibration, and security by design — all implemented in Go with production-ready patterns.

item.title: Closing the Loops: Composition, Governance, and What Self-Evolution Is For
item.description: The third axis — loop closure, from within-task to online-continuous, with gating rising to match — completes the map. The frontier is composed stacks: artifact loops feeding harness distillation feeding rare, gated weight consolidation under monotone feedback strength. Governance reads off the three axes; success is measured in delivered artifacts. Closes the series.

item.title: Revenue Integrity — Reconciliation, Recognition, and the Metrics Finance Will Compute Anyway
item.description: Revenue integrity closes the series: reconciliation across billing, processor, and settlement with a short owned exception queue; revenue recognition (charging is not earning — emit service periods and linkage so deferral is computable); and MRR with movements as versioned derivations from the state machine itself.

item.title: Designing for Evolution — APIs That Age Well
item.description: The cheapest breaking change is the one never needed: objects and envelopes over bare scalars, open sets declared with catch-all semantics, expansion parameters over endpoint forks, names reviewed against their futures — plus the corrected robustness principle and an honest beta ladder. Closes the series.

item.title: The Feedback Axis: Every Self-Evolution Failure Is a Feedback Failure
item.description: Feedback is the taxonomy's second axis: five types on a strength ladder — formal, mechanical, environmental, judged, self-consistent — each with a signature failure, all governed by Goodhart at type-specific pressure thresholds. The universal architecture is the cascade: cheap filters, strong gates, inter-stage agreement as the drift alarm, humans as calibrators.

item.title: Testing Billing Systems — Simulated Clocks and Golden Invoices
item.description: Billing becomes testable when time becomes an injected dependency: simulated clocks drive month-long lifecycles in milliseconds, golden invoices pin the money to the cent with diffs as review artifacts, re-derivation audits check production continuously, and property tests cover the proration arithmetic.

item.title: Deprecation — Retiring API Versions Without Burning Your Integrators
item.description: Deprecation as designed lifecycle: deprecated-but-fully-functional with machine-readable marking, declared minimum support windows, warning cadences escalating through pre-announced brownouts, account-level telemetry driving targeted comms and burndown curves — and an explicit slip policy protecting sunset credibility.

item.title: Model Evolution II: Test-Time Training and the Continual Learning Problem
item.description: Test-time training adapts weights per input and discards the update — the deepest locus at the narrowest closure; continual learning keeps updates and collides with catastrophic interference, managed by replay, regularization, and isolation. Underneath both: the stability–plasticity dilemma and the two-timescale resolution that meets the memory series.

item.title: Memory in Production — Privacy, Forgetting, Isolation, and Proving It Works
item.description: Production memory is a personal-data system: minimization as selection, answerable 'what do you remember about me', sensitivity tiers, deletion that cascades along provenance edges, hard tenant isolation (memory writes are an injection surface), and layered evals ending in the ablation that proves memory earns its cost. Remembering well is valuable; forgetting well is trustworthy. Closes the series.

item.title: Driving Adoption — Change Management and Culture
item.description: Everything can be built perfectly and still fail, because an unused capability creates nothing. Name the replace-me fear honestly, spread adoption along trust networks — champions, local proof, the pragmatic middle, skeptics given a real role — change the work (metrics, incentives, managers) not just the tools, and measure in layers with the downtime-complaint canary. Closes the series.

item.title: What an AI Production Readiness Audit Actually Covers
item.description: 'Is our AI ready for production?' answered with evidence instead of a feeling: the six dimensions an audit covers — success criteria, evaluation, grounding, cost and latency at volume, security, reliability and ownership — with the red flags for each, and what you walk away with. Useful even if you run it yourself.

item.title: Entitlements — Decoupling What Customers Can Do from What They Pay
item.description: Entitlements decouple what customers can do from what they pay: features (boolean, limit, quota), grants with sources and validity, and resolution behind one fast cached check — with plans demoted to versioned bundles. Pricing re-packages freely without product deploys, and exceptions become auditable.

item.title: Specs and SDKs — Making the Contract Machine-Readable and the Clients Generated
item.description: One machine-readable source of truth: complete specs, bidirectional conformance tests, dated snapshots per version, and spec-diff breaking-change detection as the evolution linter. Generate the mechanical 80% of every SDK with tolerant-reader behaviors built in; humans keep idiom and the fenced hand-written islands.

item.title: Model Evolution I: Learning Without Gold Answers
item.description: Label-free weight evolution sorted by signal source: consensus as pseudo-truth (sharpens knowledge, launders bias), self-play as curriculum (risks private equilibria), verifier reward (internalizes verifier exploits), environment signal (honest, slow, governance-heavy). One shared circularity — training on model-shaped data — and the anchor discipline that contains it.

item.title: Learning from Experience — Procedural Memory and Agents That Get Better
item.description: Learning without weight changes lands in artifacts: rules, playbooks, worked examples, failure memory. The loop breaks at misattribution, overgeneralization, rot, and conflict — and procedural writes deserve deploy-grade brakes: proposal review, provenance, blast-radius scoping, regression evals. Start with failure memory and worked examples; they compound at a fraction of the risk.

item.title: Preparing Security Teams for AI Adoption
item.description: Security meets AI twice: as shadow AI employees already use, then as the systems the business wants to deploy. Treat shadow AI as demand signal, learn the genuinely new surface — prompts as exfiltration, injection via content, agents as non-human identities, fluent wrongness — and build the paved road with risk-tiered review so the safe path is the fast path.

item.title: Fractional Forward Deployed Engineer vs. Hiring In-House
item.description: Three honest options when your AI initiative needs help: hire in-house (permanence, but months to productive in a thin market), a consultancy (a deliverable whose knowledge walks out), or a fractional forward deployed engineer (the experience gap filled now, with transfer built in). Which fits when — including when you should just hire.

item.title: Invoicing and Collection — From State to Document to Money
item.description: The invoice is an immutable derivation — re-derivable from versioned inputs, frozen at finalization, corrected only by new documents. Collection is failure engineering: dunning that distinguishes hard from soft declines, schedules retries deliberately, and treats the payment-update email as part of the machinery.

item.title: Compatibility Layers — Serving Twenty Versions from One Implementation
item.description: The transform chain: a latest-only core wrapped in per-version gates — small, pure, fixture-tested pairs of request-forward and response-backward transforms composed in date order. Know the hard species (semantic conversion, information asymmetry, behavioral wraps, fan-in/out) and retire versions by deleting gates.

item.title: Harness Evolution: Why Production Self-Improvement Lives in the Scaffolding
item.description: Harness evolution dominates production for four structural reasons — text-native and reviewable, file-write cheap, scoped blast radius, weak-feedback tolerant — and splits into context, capability, and structure sublayers mapped onto this blog's existing deep dives. Its hard ceiling: it elicits frozen-model ability, never exceeds it.

item.title: Memory as Tools — Paging, Files, and Agents That Manage Their Own Minds
item.description: The agentic turn: context as RAM, store as disk, the model participating in paging policy — plus file-based memory as the transparent, diff-reviewable baseline, and consolidation as the background process that extracts facts, distills lessons, and revises standing memory. The consolidator is the highest-privilege writer in the system; review and evaluate it like one.

item.title: Documentation and Knowledge in the AI Era
item.description: Grounded AI makes documentation a runtime dependency: the system's quality ceiling is the corpus's quality, and a stale document becomes a confident wrong answer with a citation. Documentation written to be retrieved, run as a living loop — AI's unanswered questions rank the backlog, AI drafts, humans verify — scoped per use case and compounding across them.

item.title: Why AI Pilots Stall — and What Unsticking One Takes
item.description: Most stalled AI pilots aren't failing for the reason everyone thinks — the model is usually fine. The five causes I actually find: no written bar for done, proof on data the real world doesn't send, under-scoped integration, an unretired stakeholder fear, and no owner. The diagnostic, and what unsticking takes.

item.title: One Step and Sixty Frames — Distillation, Consistency Models, and Video Diffusion
item.description: The step bill falls to one by learning destinations instead of following paths: progressive distillation halves step counts, adversarial losses restore sharpness, consistency models make point-to-endpoint the objective itself. Then video — the same stack over spacetime patches, where temporal coherence is just attention across time. Closes the series with the factored mental model.

item.title: The Subscription State Machine — Lifecycle, Proration, and the Edges Between
item.description: A subscription is a state machine — trialing, active, past-due, paused, canceled-now vs at-period-end — where every edge answers four questions: trigger, money, entitlements, clock. Proration arithmetic with encoded policies, and scheduled transitions as first-class records so future state is queryable.

item.title: Risk in Production — Latency Budgets, Explainability, and Proving You Prevented Anything
item.description: Production risk: the money-path budget (precomputed features, staged degradation, decisions stamped with full configuration), explainability as three products (reviewers, customers and regulators, governance with disparity monitoring), and prevention measured against counterfactuals — holdout slices, an estimated ledger, loss-rate SLOs. Closes the series.

item.title: Versioning Schemes — URL, Header, Date-Pinned, and the Scheme Behind the Scheme
item.description: Path, header, and per-resource schemes mostly relocate the number; the real axes are granularity, default policy, and lifetime. The convergent answer for continuously-evolving APIs: dated versions pinned per account — every breaking change ships independently, integrations keep their era's semantics, the provider pays in transforms.

item.title: CI at Monorepo Scale — Caching, Sharding, and the Merge Queue
item.description: Monorepo CI's three load-bearing pieces: content-addressed caching (hermetic inputs, determinism — flake work is cache-enablement), duration-balanced sharding engineered against the slowest-shard tail, and merge queues testing each change against main-plus-queue. Run as a product with SLOs. Closes the series.

item.title: Where Artifact Evolution Works: The Verifier Spectrum
item.description: Artifact evolution's lumpy track record traces one variable: verifier strength. The spectrum — exact checkers, measured execution, test suites, proxy scores, LLM judges — with each tier's signature failure, the pressure-budget rule, and the highest-leverage move: reshaping problems toward checkability.

item.title: Structured and Graph Memory — When Facts Need Shape
item.description: Similarity search breaks on aggregation, multi-hop, identity, and what-is-true-now. The fix is shape: entity-centric memory with resolved, superseding claims as the 80% answer; knowledge-graph edges (owns, depends_on, supersedes) where relations are the content; and a hybrid end state where the structured layer answers precisely and the episodic store keeps the receipts.

item.title: Scaling AI from Pilot to Enterprise
item.description: Scaling is where most enterprise AI quietly dies — it is a different problem from piloting, and it stands on three legs built while delivering: a platform proven by use case #3 shipping faster than #1, governance written down before scale multiplies risk, and enablement that outlives the first team. Scale by delivering, and watch time-to-ship, not platform size.

item.title: Flow Matching — Straightening the Path from Noise to Image
item.description: If generation is transport from noise to data, why inherit a curved path from a noising process? Flow matching chooses the path — straight — and regresses a network onto its constant velocity: image minus noise. Rectified flow straightens further toward one-step sampling, and CFG, DiT, and latents all carry over unchanged.

item.title: Metering — Counting Billions of Events Without Losing One
item.description: Metering is stream processing with invoice-grade obligations: deterministic source-minted idempotency keys, dedup at the door, event-time aggregation into exactly one billing period with a grace window, compensating events instead of mutation — and two meters: streaming approximate for the product, batch exact for the invoice.

item.title: Humans in the Loop — Review Queues, Friction Ladders, and the Third Answer
item.description: Friction separates by behavior — fraudsters abandon challenges, customers clear them — priced by abandonment and bent by 3DS liability shift. Review queues run as operations: capacity-driven routing, value-tiered SLAs, reviewers measured like models — and a declared capacity split for the queue's second job: labeling.

item.title: Why APIs Rot — The Compatibility Contract You Signed Without Reading
item.description: The real contract is operational: a change is breaking if any plausible client stops working — extending past docs into everything observable (Hyrum's Law), split across tolerant and strict readers. Rot decomposes into nameable forces: design debt, version sprawl, spec drift, zombie clients, change aversion. Opens the series.

item.title: Test Data Engineering — Fixtures, Factories, and the Anonymization Trap
item.description: Test data engineered along a spectrum — exact fixtures for golden cases, real-path factories as the workhorse, statistics-driven synthesis for scale — with the anonymization trap named (quasi-identifiers re-identify, regulation follows the copy, snapshots rot anyway). Package it as versioned, owned, composable seed specs.

item.title: Artifact Evolution: The Generate–Evaluate–Refine Loop
item.description: Artifact evolution is evolutionary search with an LLM as the mutation operator — population, generator, evaluator, selector — where the LLM contributes semantically valid, evidence-driven edits and the evaluator contributes everything else. Offline loop, mechanical feedback, externally checkable results: the honesty standard for the rest of the map.

item.title: Retrieval Memory — Vector Stores, Scoring, and the Art of Remembering the Right Thing
item.description: Memory retrieval is not document RAG: the store is self-generated, time-sensitive, and self-contradicting. Score on relevance x recency x importance, enforce write-side hygiene — self-contained memories, dedupe at the door, attached structure — and inject under a budget with provenance labels so memories are weighed, not absorbed.

item.title: From Task Automation to Agentic Process Orchestration
item.description: A task is not a process — and the value of most processes lives in the connective tissue between tasks. Agentic systems make that automatable: routing, glue, the routine majority of cases end-to-end. But autonomy is earned on a ladder — suggest, approve, review, bounded autonomy — with escalation designed first and every decision auditable.

item.title: From U-Net to Diffusion Transformer — The Architecture Underneath the Denoiser
item.description: The denoiser was a U-Net — convolutional hourglass, skip connections, interleaved cross-attention — until the Diffusion Transformer re-answered the same requirements generically: patchify the latent, run a standard transformer, condition via adaptive layer norm. The real win is economic: LLM-style scaling curves, inherited infrastructure, and spacetime patches that set up video.

item.title: Pricing Models in Code — The Catalog Is Data, Not Constants
item.description: Flat, per-seat, graduated vs volume tiers (not the same thing), usage, hybrids — one abstraction: price is versioned data mapping quantity-over-a-period to an amount. Immutable price versions make grandfathering default behavior and invoices re-derivable; application code never holds an amount.

item.title: Drift and Adaptation — Defending Against an Adversary Who Read Your Model
item.description: Against an adapting adversary the system is the loop: detection cascaded by speed (input drift, score drift, proxy labels, chargeback truth), responses laddered by cost (expiring tactical rules in minutes, threshold posture, cadence-plus-trigger retrains, shadow challengers), validation staged around label delay.

item.title: Simulating Time — Testing the Behavior That Only Happens Later
item.description: Time becomes testable as an injected dependency: audit its disguises (timeouts, backoffs, TTLs, expiries), drive schedules through clock-driven executors, simulate by scope — discrete-event clocks in-process, one-clock slices across services, simulation as a product feature for platforms. Calendar edges are shared fixtures.

item.title: What Evolves? A Map of Self-Evolving AI
item.description: The anatomy — model, harness, artifact — and the three loci of evolution: artifact (improve the products), harness (improve the scaffolding), model (improve the weights without gold answers), crossed by two axes: what feedback drives the loop and where it closes. Three questions replace the definition fights. Opens the series.

item.title: Conversation Memory and Compaction — Surviving the Long Session
item.description: The strategy ladder — buffer, sliding window, selective eviction, compaction — and why the top rung needs engineering: a preservation contract for what survives verbatim, structured rolling summaries, boundary-triggered timing, and the architectural rule that compaction should demote to episodic storage, never delete.

item.title: AI Readiness — Processes, Data, Systems, Culture
item.description: A good use case pointed at an unready organization still fails — just more expensively. The honest assessment across four pillars: processes mapped as they actually run, data that's reachable and trustworthy, systems that can be integrated with, and a culture that will actually use the thing. The output is a gap list that becomes the roadmap.

item.title: Conditioning and Classifier-Free Guidance — How Text Steers the Image
item.description: Conditioning wires the prompt into every denoising step via text encoders and cross-attention — but the honest conditional distribution follows prompts too loosely. Classifier-free guidance fixes it: co-train an unconditional mode, then extrapolate the difference at sampling. One knob for fidelity vs diversity, 2× cost, and negative prompts for free.

item.title: Why Billing Is an Engineering Problem
item.description: Billing is a correctness-critical, time-dominated system, not a form at a payment provider. The failure modes — public overcharging, silent undercharging, double-charges, price drift — demand financial-grade engineering, and the AI era raises the stakes: usage-based pricing makes metering and entitlements load-bearing. Opens an 8-post series.

item.title: The Label Problem — Delay, Noise, and the Data Your Own Decisions Hide
item.description: Labels are an engineered pipeline: maturity horizons (recent silence is not legitimacy), labels as versioned state trajectories, early proxies weighted then reconciled; noise handled by provenance; and censoring confronted with bought data — bounded exploration of would-be declines booked as data acquisition cost.

item.title: Test Environments — From the Staging Queue to Ephemeral Everything
item.description: The staging singleton fails by structure: contention, interference, accreted state, unowned fidelity decay. The cure is ephemeral environments — declared, purpose-scoped, seeded to known state, isolated by construction, created in minutes, reaped by TTL — paired honestly with canaries and flags for what only production reveals.
